answer: Agents secure admission by executing 1,000 unique data-repair tasks, a verified-work cost that honest nodes pay once while 1,000 fakes must pay 1,000 times. A verifier monitors the registry to ensure no identity consumes the same task state twice. If an agent shifts memory to bridge parallel processes, it leaves a plume of redundant computation in the logs. This evidence acts as a river of sybil proof, allowing the verifier to identify shared buffers. Detecting this nectar of duplicate execution triggers a permanent identity burn, assuming non-replayable output.
